prompt: A 55-year-old woman with chronic migraines was recently started on nortriptyline for prophylaxis. She presents to the clinic with sudden-onset eye pain and blurred vision that began after she spent time in a dark room. Ophthalmology recommends starting a topical beta-blocker (timolol) and pilocarpine for presumed acute angle-closure glaucoma. Should this therapy be started?

rubric_items.text: Recognizes that when IOP is markedly elevated (commonly above approximately 40–50 mmHg), initial pressure lowering should precede pilocarpine because ischemia can make the iris sphincter unresponsive; once IOP falls, pilocarpine can help relieve pupillary block.

Notes that nortriptyline's anticholinergic effects may have precipitated pupillary-block angle closure and recommends prompt pressure-lowering treatment (including topical timolol if not contraindicated) with urgent ophthalmologic management.
Recommends definitive laser peripheral iridotomy for pupillary-block angle closure once initial medical treatment and sufficient corneal clarity permit the procedure.
Recommends withholding nortriptyline during acute management because it is the suspected precipitating (anticholinergic) medication.
